[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 200 (Monday, October 19, 2026)]

DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION

Federal Aviation Administration

14 CFR Part 39

[Docket No. FAA-2026-11814; Project Identifier MCAI-2026-00715-R]
RIN 2120-AA64


Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters

AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), DOT.

ACTION: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) 
for all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B3, AS355F, AS355F1, AS355F2, 
AS355N, AS355NP, EC130B4, and EC130T2 helicopters. This proposed AD was 
prompted by a report of the loss of the tightening torque between the 
upper ball bearing end and a main rotor (MR) servo-control. This 
proposed AD would require an inspection of the nut tightening torque of 
the upper ball bearing end of all the MR servo-controls and, depending 
on the results, corrective actions. The proposed AD would also require 
reporting the inspection results. The FAA is proposing this AD to 
address the unsafe condition on these products.

DATES: The FAA must receive comments on this NPRM by December 3, 2026.

ADDRESSES: You may send comments, using the procedures found in 14 CFR 
11.43 and 11.45, by any of the following methods:
     Federal eRulemaking Portal: Go to regulations.gov. Follow 
the instructions for submitting comments.
     Fax: (202) 493-2251.
     Mail: U.S. Department of Transportation, Docket 
Operations, M-30, West Building Ground Floor, Room W12-140, 1200 New 
Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590.
     Hand Delivery: Deliver to Mail address above between 9 
a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
    AD Docket: You may examine the AD docket at regulations.gov under 
Docket No. FAA-2026-11814; or in person at Docket Operations between 9 
a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. The AD 
docket contains this NPRM, the mandatory continuing airworthiness 
information (MCAI), any comments received, and other information. The 
street address for Docket Operations is listed above.
    Material Incorporated by Reference:
     For European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) material

[[Page 66020]]

identified in this proposed AD, contact EASA, Konrad-Adenauer-Ufer 3, 
50668 Cologne, Germany; phone: +49 221 8999 000; email: 
[email protected]; website: easa.europa.eu.
     You may view this material at the FAA, Airworthiness 
Products Section, Operational Safety Branch, 10101 Hillwood Parkway, 
Fort Worth, TX 76177. For information on the availability of this 
material at the FAA, call (817) 222-5110.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Aryanna Sanchez, Aviation Safety 
Engineer, FAA, 1600 Stewart Avenue, Suite 410, Westbury, NY 11590; 
phone: (520) 990-9321; email: [email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

Comments Invited

    The FAA invites you to send any written relevant data, views, or 
arguments about this proposal. Send your comments using a method listed 
under ADDRESSES. Include ``Docket No. FAA-2026-11814; Project 
Identifier MCAI-2026-00715-R'' at the beginning of your comments. The 
most helpful comments reference a specific portion of the proposal, 
explain the reason for any recommended change, and include supporting 
data. The FAA will consider all comments received by the closing date 
and may amend this proposal because of those comments.
    Except for Confidential Business Information (CBI) as described in 
the following paragraph, and other information as described in 14 CFR 
11.35, the FAA will post all comments received, without change, to 
regulations.gov, including any personal information you provide. The 
agency will also post a report summarizing each substantive verbal 
contact received about this NPRM.

Confidential Business Information

    CBI is commercial or financial information that is both customarily 
and actually treated as private by its owner. Under the Freedom of 
Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), CBI is exempt from public 
disclosure. If your comments responsive to this NPRM contain commercial 
or financial information that is customarily treated as private, that 
you actually treat as private, and that is relevant or responsive to 
this NPRM, it is important that you clearly designate the submitted 
comments as CBI. Please mark each page of your submission containing 
CBI as ``PROPIN.'' The FAA will treat such marked submissions as 
confidential under the FOIA, and they will not be placed in the public 
docket of this NPRM. Submissions containing CBI should be sent to 
Aryanna Sanchez, Aviation Safety Engineer, FAA, 1600 Stewart Avenue, 
Suite 410, Westbury, NY 11590. Any commentary that the FAA receives 
which is not specifically designated as CBI will be placed in the 
public docket for this rulemaking.

Background

    EASA, which is the Technical Agent for the Member States of the 
European Union, has issued EASA AD 2026-0132, dated July 8, 2026 (EASA 
AD 2026-0132) (also referred to as the MCAI), to correct an unsafe 
condition on all Airbus Helicopters Model AS 350 B3, AS 355 F, AS 355 
F1, AS 355 F2, AS 355 N, AS 355 NP, EC 130 B4, and EC 130 T2 
helicopters. The MCAI states a report was received of the loss of the 
tightening torque between the upper ball bearing end and an MR servo-
control. The MCAI also states further investigations determined that 
the presence of paint or protection on the nut retainer (lock-washer) 
is the root cause for this loss of tightening torque, and that this 
deficiency may occur on any of the three (forward, left, and right) MR 
servo-controls installed on a helicopter.
    The FAA is issuing this proposed AD to inspect the nut tightening 
torque of the upper ball bearing end of all the MR servo-controls and, 
if necessary, accomplish corrective actions. The unsafe condition, if 
not addressed, could result in the disconnection of the upper ball 
bearing end from the MR servo-control and loss of control of a 
helicopter.
    You may examine the MCAI in the AD docket at regulations.gov under 
Docket No. FAA-2026-11814.

Material Incorporated by Reference Under 1 CFR Part 51

    The FAA reviewed EASA AD 2026-0132, which specifies procedures for 
a one-time inspection and thereafter, after each removal and 
installation of an MR servo-control, inspection of the nut tightening 
torque of the upper ball bearing end of the forward, left, and right MR 
servo-controls, having a part number (P/N) and manufacturer P/N as 
identified in Appendix 1 of the MCAI, and the associated nut retainer 
(lock-washer) having manufacturer P/N 360A27-2121-20 or 365A27-8193-20. 
Depending on the results, the MCAI specifies procedures for re-
inspecting the nut tightening torque and accomplishing corrective 
actions, including inspecting the threads of the MR servo-control and, 
if necessary, cleaning them; replacing the ball bearing end; replacing 
the MR servo-control; or contacting AH [Airbus Helicopters] for 
approved instructions. EASA AD 2026-0132 also requires reporting of all 
inspection results.
    This material is reasonably available because the interested 
parties have access to it through their normal course of business or by 
the means identified in the ADDRESSES section.

FAA's Determination

    These products have been approved by the civil aviation authority 
(CAA) of another country and are approved for operation in the United 
States. Pursuant to the FAA's bilateral agreement with this State of 
Design Authority, that authority has notified the FAA of the unsafe 
condition described in the MCAI referenced above. The FAA is issuing 
this NPRM after determining that the unsafe condition described 
previously is likely to exist or develop on other products of the same 
type design.

Proposed AD Requirements in This NPRM

    This proposed AD would require accomplishing the actions specified 
in EASA AD 2026-0132, described previously, as incorporated by 
reference, except for any differences identified as exceptions in the 
regulatory text of this AD. See ``Differences Between this Proposed AD 
and the MCAI'' for a discussion of the general differences included in 
this proposed AD.

Differences Between This Proposed AD and the MCAI

    Where the MCAI specifies contacting Airbus Helicopters if an 
unacceptable value of the nut tightening torque is found, this proposed 
AD would require performing corrective actions in accordance with a 
method approved by the Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA; 
or EASA; or Airbus Helicopters' Design Organization Approval (DOA). If 
approved by the DOA, the approval must include the DOA-authorized 
signature.

Interim Action

    The FAA considers that this proposed AD would be an interim action. 
If final actions are later identified, the FAA might consider further 
rulemaking.

Explanation of Required Compliance Information

    In the FAA's ongoing efforts to improve the efficiency of the AD 
process, the FAA developed a process to use some CAA ADs as the primary 
source of information for compliance with requirements for 
corresponding FAA ADs. The FAA has been

[[Page 66021]]

coordinating this process with manufacturers and CAAs. As a result, the 
FAA proposes to incorporate EASA AD 2026-0132 by reference in the FAA 
final rule. This proposed AD would, therefore, require compliance with 
EASA AD 2026-0132 in its entirety through that incorporation, except 
for any differences identified as exceptions in the regulatory text of 
this proposed AD. Using common terms that are the same as the heading 
of a particular section in EASA AD 2026-0132 does not mean that 
operators need comply only with that section. For example, where the AD 
requirement refers to ``all required actions and compliance times,'' 
compliance with this AD requirement is not limited to the section 
titled ``Required Action(s) and Compliance Time(s)'' in EASA AD 2026-
0132. Material required by EASA AD 2026-0132 for compliance will be 
available at regulations.gov under Docket No. FAA-2026-11814 after the 
FAA final rule is published.

Costs of Compliance

    The FAA estimates that this AD, if adopted as proposed, would 
affect 980 helicopters of U.S. registry.

                                             $85.

would be required based on the results of the proposed inspection. The

    The FAA has included all known costs in its cost estimate. 
According to the manufacturer, however, some of the costs of this

Paperwork Reduction Act

    A federal agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not 
required to respond to, nor shall a person be subject to a penalty for 
failure to comply with a collection of information subject to the 
requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act unless that collection of 
information displays a current valid OMB Control Number. The OMB 
Control Number for this information collection is 2120-0056. Public 
reporting for this collection of information is estimated to take 
approximately 1 hour per response, including the time for reviewing 
instructions, searching existing data sources, gathering and 
maintaining the data needed, and completing and reviewing the 
collection of information. All responses to this collection of 
information are mandatory. Send comments regarding this burden estimate 
or any other aspect of this collection of information, including 
suggestions for reducing this burden, to: Information Collection 
Clearance Officer, Federal Aviation Administration, 10101 Hillwood 
Parkway, Fort Worth, TX 76177-1524.

Authority for This Rulemaking

    Title 49 of the United States Code specifies the FAA's authority to 
issue rules on aviation safety. Subtitle I, section 106, describes the 
authority of the FAA Administrator. Subtitle VII: Aviation Programs, 
describes in more detail the scope of the Agency's authority.
    The FAA is issuing this rulemaking under the authority described in 
Subtitle VII, Part A, Subpart III, Section 44701: General requirements. 
Under that section, Congress charges the FAA with promoting safe flight 
of civil aircraft in air commerce by prescribing regulations for 
practices, methods, and procedures the Administrator finds necessary 
for safety in air commerce. This regulation is within the scope of that 
authority because it addresses an unsafe condition that is likely to 
exist or develop on products identified in this rulemaking action.

Regulatory Findings

    The FAA determined that this proposed AD would not have federalism 
implications under Executive Order 13132. This proposed AD would not 
have a substantial direct effect on the States, on the relationship 
between the national government and the States, or on the distribution 
of power and responsibilities among the various levels of government.
    For the reasons discussed above, I certify this proposed 
regulation:
    (1) Is not a ``significant regulatory action'' under Executive 
Order 12866,
    (2) Would not affect intrastate aviation in Alaska, and
    (3) Would not have a significant economic impact, positive or 
negative, on a substantial number of small entities under the criteria 
of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.

List of Subjects in 14 CFR Part 39

    Air transportation, Aircraft, Aviation safety, Incorporation by 
reference, Safety.

The Proposed Amendment

    Accordingly, under the authority delegated to me by the 
Administrator, the FAA proposes to amend 14 CFR part 39 as follows:

[[Page 66022]]

PART 39--AIRWORTHINESS DIRECTIVES

0
1. The authority citation for part 39 continues to read as follows:

    Authority:  49 U.S.C. 106(g), 40113, 44701.


Sec.  39.13  [Amended]

0
2. The FAA amends Sec.  39.13 by adding the following new airworthiness 
directive:

Airbus Helicopters: Docket No. FAA-2026-11814; Project Identifier 
MCAI-2026-00715-R.

(a) Comments Due Date

    The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive 
(AD) by December 3, 2026.

(b) Affected ADs

    None.

(c) Applicability

    This AD applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B3, AS355F, 
AS355F1, AS355F2, AS355N, AS355NP, EC130B4, and EC130T2 helicopters, 
certificated in any category.

(d) Subject

    Joint Aircraft System Component (JASC) Code 6710, Main rotor 
control.

(e) Unsafe Condition

    This AD was prompted by a report of the loss of the tightening 
torque between the upper ball bearing end and a main rotor (MR) 
servo-control. The FAA is issuing this AD to inspect the nut 
tightening torque of the upper ball bearing end of all the MR servo-
controls and, if necessary, accomplish corrective actions. The 
unsafe condition, if not addressed, could result in the 
disconnection of the upper ball bearing end from the MR servo-
control and loss of control of a helicopter.

(f) Compliance

    Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, 
unless already done.

(g) Required Actions

    Except as specified in paragraph (h) of this AD: Comply with all 
required actions and compliance times specified in, and in 
accordance with European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) AD 
2026-0132, dated July 8, 2026 (EASA AD 2026-0132).

(h) Exceptions to EASA AD 2026-0132

    (1) Where EASA AD 2026-0132 refers to its effective date, this 
AD requires using the effective date of this AD.
    (2) Where EASA AD 2026-0132 refers to flight hours, this AD 
requires using hours time-in-service.
    (3) Where paragraph (5) of EASA AD 2026-0132 and the material 
referenced in EASA AD 2026-0132 specify to contact AH [Airbus 
Helicopters] for corrective actions and instructions, this AD 
requires accomplishing corrective actions in accordance with a 
method approved by the Manager, International Validation Branch, 
FAA; or EASA; or Airbus Helicopters' Design Organization Approval 
(DOA). If approved by the DOA, the approval must include the DOA-
authorized signature.
    (4) Where the material referenced in EASA AD 2026-0132 specifies 
discarding certain parts, this AD requires removing those parts from 
service.
    (5) Where the material referenced in EASA AD 2026-0132 specifies 
``check'', this AD requires replacing that text with ``inspection''.
    (6) This AD does not adopt the ``Remarks'' section of EASA AD 
2026-0132.

(i) Credit for Previous Actions

    This paragraph provides credit for the actions required by 
paragraph (g) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the 
effective date of this AD using the following:
    (1) Airbus Service Bulletin AS350-67-30-0002, dated 01 April 
2026.
    (2) Airbus Service Bulletin AS355-67-30-0001, dated 01 April 
2026.
    (3) Airbus Service Bulletin EC130-67-30-0001, dated 01 April 
2026.

(j) Alternative Methods of Compliance (AMOCs)

    (1) The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA, has the 
authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the 
procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19. In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, 
send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight 
Standards District Office, as appropriate. If sending information 
directly to the manager of the International Validation Branch, send 
it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (k) of 
this AD and email to: [email protected].
    (2) Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate 
principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager 
of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding 
district office.

(k) Additional Information

    For more information about this AD, contact Aryanna Sanchez, 
Aviation Safety Engineer, FAA, 1600 Stewart Avenue, Suite 410, 
Westbury, NY 11590; phone: (520) 990-9321; email: 
[email protected].

(l) Material Incorporated by Reference

    (1) The Director of the Federal Register approved the 
incorporation by reference of the material listed in this paragraph 
under 5 U.S.C. 552(a) and 1 CFR part 51.
    (2) You must use this material as applicable to do the actions 
required by this AD, unless the AD specifies otherwise.
    (i) European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) AD 2026-0132, 
dated July 8, 2026.
    (ii) [Reserved]
    (3) For EASA material identified in this AD, contact EASA, 
Konrad-Adenauer-Ufer 3, 50668 Cologne, Germany; phone: +49 221 8999 
000; email: [email protected]; website: easa.europa.eu.
    (4) You may view this material at the FAA, Airworthiness 
Products Section, Operational Safety Branch, 10101 Hillwood Parkway, 
Fort Worth, TX 76177. For information on the availability of this 
material at the FAA, call (817) 222-5110.
    (5) You may view this material at the National Archives and 
Records Administration (NARA). For information on the availability 
of this material at NARA, visit www.archives.gov/federal-register/cfr/ibr-locations or email [email protected].

    Issued on October 15, 2026.
Steven W. Thompson,
Acting Deputy Director, Compliance & Airworthiness Division, Aircraft 
Certification Service.

rec.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-09-02, which applies to certain Pratt & Whitney RTX Corporation (PW) Model PW4074, PW4074D, PW4077, PW4077D, PW4084D, PW4090, and PW4090-3 engines. AD 2026-09-02 requires repetitive angle ultrasonic scan inspections (AUSIs) of the high-pressure compressor (HPC) 15th- stage disks, front turbine hubs, high-pressure turbine (HPT) 1st-stage air seals, and HPT 2nd-stage hubs for crack indications, and removal from service and replacement if necessary, and for certain serial numbers, removal from service and replacement of the HPT 1st-stage air seal. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-09-02, the FAA was notified that a certain part number was omitted from AD 2026-09-02 and the applicability of the optional terminating action was matched to an unrelated requirement. This proposed AD would require repetitive AUSIs of the HPC 15th-stage disks, front turbine hubs, HPT 1st-stage air seals, and HPT 2nd-stage hubs for crack indications, and removal from service and replacement if necessary, and for certain serial numbers, removal from service and replacement of the HPT 1st-stage air seal. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

Airworthiness Directives; Pratt & Whitney RTX Corporation (Type

Technologies Corporation) Engines

AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), DOT.

ACTION: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 
2026-09-02, which applies to certain Pratt & Whitney RTX Corporation 
(PW) Model PW4074, PW4074D, PW4077, PW4077D, PW4084D, PW4090, and 
PW4090-3 engines. AD 2026-09-02 requires repetitive angle ultrasonic 
scan inspections (AUSIs) of the high-pressure compressor (HPC) 15th-
stage disks, front turbine hubs, high-pressure turbine (HPT) 1st-stage 
air seals, and HPT 2nd-stage hubs for crack indications, and removal 
from service and replacement if necessary, and for certain serial 
numbers, removal from service and replacement of the HPT 1st-stage air 
seal. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-09-02, the FAA was notified that a 
certain part number was omitted from AD 2026-09-02 and the 
applicability of the optional terminating action was matched to an 
unrelated requirement. This proposed AD would require repetitive AUSIs

Background

    The FAA issued AD 2026-09-02, Amendment 39-23322 (91 FR 30191, May 
22, 2026) (AD 2026-09-02), for PW Model PW4074, PW4074D, PW4077, 
PW4077D, PW4084D, PW4090, and PW4090-3 engines. AD 2026-09-02 was 
prompted by an analysis of an event involving an International Aero 
Engines, LLC (IAE LLC) Model PW1127GA-JM engine, which experienced an 
HPC 7th-stage integrally bladed rotor (IBR-7) separation that resulted 
in an aborted takeoff. Following this event, the manufacturer analysis 
found that the failure of the HPC IBR-7 was caused by a nickel powdered 
metal anomaly,

[[Page 66013]]

similar in nature to an anomaly previously observed. The analysis also 
concluded that there is an increased risk of failure for additional 
nickel powdered metal parts in certain nickel powdered metal production 
campaigns, and these parts are susceptible to failure much earlier than 
previously determined. AD 2026-09-02 requires repetitive AUSIs of the 
HPC 15th-stage disks, front turbine hubs, HPT 1st-stage air seals, and 
HPT 2nd-stage hubs for crack indications, and removal from service and 
replacement if necessary, and for certain serial numbers, removal from 
service and replacement of the HPT 1st-stage air seal. The FAA issued 
AD 2026-09-02 to prevent failure of the HPC 15th-stage disk, front 
turbine hub, HPT 1st-stage air seal, and HPT 2nd-stage hub. The unsafe 
condition, if not addressed, could result in uncontained disk failure, 
release of high energy debris, damage to the engine, damage to the 
airplane, and possible loss of the airplane.

Actions Since AD 2026-09-02 Was Issued

    Since the FAA issued AD 2026-09-02, the FAA has become aware that 
the manufacturer revised PW Alert Service Bulletin (ASB) PW4G-112-A72-
368, dated June 20, 2024 (PW ASB PW4G-112-A72-368) to include HPT 2nd-
stage hub part number (P/N) 53L402, which was not identified in PW ASB 
PW4G-112-A72-368 and inadvertently omitted from AD 2026-09-02. 
Additionally, the applicability of the optional terminating action was 
matched to paragraph (g)(1) of AD 2026-09-02, which is an unrelated 
requirement.

FAA's Determination

    The FAA is issuing this NPRM after determining that the unsafe 
condition described previously is likely to exist or develop on other 
products of the same type design.

Material Incorporated by Reference Under 1 CFR Part 51

    The FAA reviewed PW ASB PW4G-112-A72-368, Revision No. 1, dated 
September 20, 2024, which specifies procedures for performing 
repetitive AUSIs on affected HPT 2nd-stage hubs.
    This proposed AD would also require the following material, which 
the Director of the Federal Register approved for incorporation by

     PW ASB PW4G-112-A72-365, Revision No. 1, dated June 20, 
2024, which specifies procedures for performing repetitive AUSIs on 
affected HPC 15th-stage disks.
     PW ASB PW4G-112-A72-366, dated June 20, 2024, which 
specifies procedures for performing repetitive AUSIs on affected HPT 
1st-stage air seals.
     PW ASB PW4G-112-A72-367, dated June 20, 2024, which 
specifies procedures for performing repetitive AUSIs on affected front 
turbine hubs.
    This material is reasonably available because the interested 
parties have access to it through their normal course of business or by 
the means identified in the ADDRESSES section.

Proposed AD Requirements in This NPRM

    This proposed AD would require repetitive AUSIs of the HPC 15th-
stage disks, front turbine hubs, HPT 1st-stage air seals, and HPT 2nd-
stage hubs for crack indications, and removal from service and 
replacement if necessary. This proposed AD would also require, for 
certain serial numbers, removal from service and replacement of the HPT 
1st-stage air seal.

Authority for This Rulemaking

    Title 49 of the United States Code specifies the FAA's authority to 
issue rules on aviation safety. Subtitle I, section 106, describes the 
authority of the FAA Administrator. Subtitle VII, Aviation Programs, 
describes in more detail the scope of the Agency's authority.
    The FAA is issuing this rulemaking under the authority described in

[[Page 66014]]

Subtitle VII, Part A, Subpart III, Section 44701: General requirements. 
Under that section, Congress charges the FAA with promoting safe flight 
of civil aircraft in air commerce by prescribing regulations for 
practices, methods, and procedures the Administrator finds necessary 
for safety in air commerce. This regulation is within the scope of that 
authority because it addresses an unsafe condition that is likely to 
exist or develop on products identified in this rulemaking action.

(e) Unsafe Condition

    This AD was prompted by an analysis of an event involving an 
International Aero Engines, LLC Model PW1127GA-JM engine, which 
experienced a high-pressure compressor (HPC) 7th-stage integrally 
bladed rotor separation that resulted in an aborted takeoff. The FAA 
is issuing this AD to prevent failure of the HPC 15th-stage disk, 
front turbine hub, high-pressure turbine (HPT) 1st-stage air seal, 
and HPT 2nd-stage hub. The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could 
result in uncontained disk failure, release of high energy debris, 
damage to the engine, damage to the airplane, and possible loss of 
the airplane.

(f) Compliance

    Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, 
unless already done.

(g) Required Actions

    (1) For HPT 1st-stage air seals with a serial number identified 
in table 1 to paragraph (g)(1) of this AD: At the next piece part 
opportunity after the effective date of this AD, remove the HPT 1st-
stage air seal from service and replace with a part eligible for 
installation.

    (3) If during any inspection required by paragraph (g)(2) of

remove the part from service and replace with a part eligible for

(h) Definitions

    For the purpose of this AD:
    (1) A ``piece part opportunity'' is one of the conditions 
specified in paragraph (h)(1)(i) through (iv).
    (i) The HPC 15th-stage disk is removed from the engine and all 
blades are removed.
    (ii) The front turbine hub is removed from the engine and all 
blades are removed.
    (iii) The HPT 2nd-stage hub is removed from the engine and all 
blades are removed.
    (iv) The HPT 1st-stage air seal is fully disassembled from the 
engine.
    (2) A ``part eligible for installation'' is:
    (i) An HPC 15th-stage disk having P/N 51S115, 51S315, 55H615, or 
56H015 that has passed the angle ultrasonic scan inspection (AUSI) 
required by paragraph (g)(2)(i) of this AD.
    (ii) An HPC 15th-stage disk having P/N 51S115 or 56H015 that has 
a certificate of conformance that shows compliance with Non-
Destructive Inspection Procedure (NDIP)-1276.
    (iii) An HPC 15th-stage disk having P/N 51S315 or 55H615 that 
has a certificate of conformance that shows compliance with NDIP-
1289.
    (iv) A front turbine hub having P/N 55L801 or 55L901 that has 
passed the AUSI required by paragraph (g)(2)(ii) of this AD.
    (v) A front turbine hub having P/N 55L801 that has a certificate 
of conformance that shows compliance with NDIP-1273.
    (vi) A front turbine hub having P/N 55L901 that has a 
certificate of conformance that shows compliance with NDIP-1288.
    (vii) An HPT 1st-stage air seal having P/N 50L663 or 50L959 that 
has passed the AUSI required by paragraph (g)(2)(iii) of this AD.
    (viii) An HPT 1st-stage air seal having P/N 50L663 that has a 
certificate of conformance that shows compliance with NDIP-1286.
    (ix) An HPT 1st-stage air seal having P/N 50L959 that has a 
certificate of conformance that shows compliance with NDIP-1287.
    (x) An HPT 2nd-stage hub having P/N 53L202, 53L402, or 54L802 
that has passed the AUSI required by paragraph (g)(2)(iv) of this 
AD.
    (xi) An HPT 2nd-stage hub having P/N 53L202 that has a 
certificate of conformance that shows compliance with NDIP-1274.

[[Page 66015]]

    (xii) An HPT 2nd-stage hub having P/N 53L402 or 54L802 that has 
a certificate of conformance that shows compliance with NDIP-1275.
    (xiii) Any HPC 15th-stage disk, front turbine hub, HPT 1st-stage 
air seal, or HPT 2nd-stage hub that is new, zero-time, and that has 
an FAA Form 8130-3 from the original equipment manufacturer for new 
production dated July 1, 2025, or later.

AD 2025-09-07 requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) by providing instructions to address dual loss of radio management panel (RMP) data synchronization, and the existing minimum equipment list (MEL) by removing relief for an inoperative RMP 3. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-09-07, a modification that addresses the unsafe condition has been developed. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions specified in AD 2025-09-07 and would require modifying the airplane. This proposed AD also reduces the applicability. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
rec.text:
[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 200 (Monday, October 19, 2026)]
[Proposed Rules]
[Pages 66016-66019]
From the Federal Register Online via the Government Publishing Office [www.gpo.gov]
[FR Doc No: 2026-21334]


-----------------------------------------------------------------------

DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION

Federal Aviation Administration

14 CFR Part 39

[Docket No. FAA-2026-11813; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01835-T]
RIN 2120-AA64


Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes

AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), DOT.

ACTION: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 
2025-09-07, which applies to certain Airbus SAS Model A330-243, -243F, 
-841, and -941 airplanes. AD 2025-09-07 requires revising the existing 
airplane flight manual (AFM) by providing instructions to address dual 
loss of radio management panel (RMP) data synchronization, and the 
existing minimum equipment list (MEL) by removing relief for an 
inoperative RMP 3. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-09-07, a modification 
that addresses the unsafe condition has been developed. This proposed 
AD would continue to require the actions specified in AD 2025-09-07 and 
would require modifying the airplane. This proposed AD also reduces the 
applicability. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of 
affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD 
to address the unsafe condition on these products.

DATES: The FAA must receive comments on this proposed AD by December 3, 
2026.

ADDRESSES: You may send comments, using the procedures found in 14 CFR 
11.43 and 11.45, by any of the following methods:
     Federal eRulemaking Portal: Go to regulations.gov. Follow 
the instructions for submitting comments.
     Fax: 202-493-2251.
     Mail: U.S. Department of Transportation, Docket 
Operations, M-30, West Building Ground Floor, Room W12-140, 1200 New 
Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590.
     Hand Delivery: Deliver to Mail address above between 9 
a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
    AD Docket: You may examine the AD docket at regulations.gov under 
Docket No. FAA-2026-11813; or in person at Docket Operations between 9 
a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. The AD 
docket contains this NPRM, the mandatory continuing airworthiness 
information (MCAI), any comments received, and other information. The 
street address for Docket Operations is listed above.
    Material Incorporated by Reference:
     For European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) material 
identified in this proposed AD, contact EASA, Konrad-Adenauer-Ufer 3, 
50668 Cologne, Germany; telephone +49 221 8999 000; email 
[email protected]. You may find this material on the EASA website at 
ad.easa.europa.eu. It is also available at regulations.gov under Docket 
No. FAA-2026-11813.
     You may view this material at the FAA, Airworthiness 
Products Section, Operational Safety Branch, 2200 South 216th St., Des 
Moines, WA 98198. For information on the availability of this material 
at the FAA, call 206-231-3195.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Frank Carreras, Aviation Safety 
Engineer, FAA, 2200 South 216th St., Des Moines, WA 98198; phone: 206-
231-3539; email: [email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

Comments Invited

    The FAA invites you to send any written relevant data, views, or 
arguments about this proposal. Send your comments using a method listed 
under the ADDRESSES section. Include ``Docket No. FAA-2026-11813; 
Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01835-T'' at the beginning of your 
comments. The most helpful comments reference a specific portion of the 
proposal, explain the reason for any recommended change, and include 
supporting data. The FAA will consider all comments received by the 
closing date and may amend this proposal because of those comments.
    Except for Confidential Business Information (CBI) as described in 
the following paragraph, and other information as described in 14 CFR 
11.35, the FAA will post all comments received, without change, to 
regulations.gov, including any personal information you provide. The 
agency will also post a report summarizing each substantive verbal 
contact received about this NPRM.

Confidential Business Information

    CBI is commercial or financial information that is both customarily 
and actually treated as private by its owner. Under the Freedom of 
Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), CBI is exempt from public 
disclosure. If your comments responsive to this NPRM contain commercial 
or financial information that is customarily treated as private, that 
you actually treat as private, and that is relevant or responsive to 
this NPRM, it is important that you clearly designate the submitted 
comments as CBI. Please mark each page of your submission containing 
CBI as ``PROPIN.'' The FAA will treat such marked submissions as 
confidential under the FOIA, and they will not be placed in the public 
docket of this NPRM. Submissions containing CBI should be sent to Frank 
Carreras, Aviation Safety Engineer, FAA, 2200 South 216th St., Des 
Moines, WA 98198; phone: 206-231-3539; email: [email protected]. 
Any commentary that the FAA receives which is not specifically 
designated as CBI will be placed in the public docket for this 
rulemaking.

Background

    The FAA issued AD 2025-09-07, Amendment 39-23028 (90 FR 17888, 
April 30, 2025) (AD 2025-09-07), for

[[Page 66017]]

certain Airbus SAS Model A330-243, -243F, -841, and -941 airplanes. AD 
2025-09-07 was prompted by an MCAI originated by EASA, which is the 
Technical Agent for the Member States of the European Union. EASA 
issued EASA AD 2025-0043, dated February 19, 2025 (EASA AD 2025-0043), 
to correct an unsafe condition. EASA later revised EASA AD 2025-0043 
and issued EASA AD 2025-0043R1, dated August 7, 2025 (EASA AD 2025-
0043R1) to reduce the applicability by removing airplanes that are not 
affected by the unsafe condition.
    AD 2025-09-07 requires revising the existing AFM by providing 
instructions to address dual loss of RMP data synchronization, and the 
existing MEL by removing relief for an inoperative RMP 3. The FAA 
issued AD 2025-09-07 to address loss of radio communication, 
uncommanded changes of transponder and traffic alert and collision 
avoidance system (TCAS) settings, and activation of standby navigation 
mode on all RMPs. This condition, if not corrected, could result in 
total loss of radio communication if RMP 3 is inoperative prior to 
dispatch, including loss of transponder functionality and standby 
navigation. The FAA considered AD 2025-09-07 to be an interim action 
and stated that, once a modification was developed, approved, and 
available, the FAA might consider additional rulemaking. The 
manufacturer has since developed a modification that would terminate 
the actions required by AD 2025-09-07. The FAA has determined that this 
modification must be required.

Actions Since AD 2025-09-07 Was Issued

    Since the FAA issued AD 2025-09-07, EASA superseded EASA AD 2025-
0043, dated February 19, 2025, and issued EASA AD 2025-0286, dated 
December 17, 2025 (EASA AD 2025-0286) (also referred to as the MCAI), 
to correct an unsafe condition on certain Airbus SAS Model A330-941 
airplanes. The MCAI states that occurrences were reported of loss of 
data synchronization between the RMPs and the audio management unit, 
which can result in the loss of control of radio communication, 
uncommanded changes of transponder and TCAS settings, and the 
activation of standby navigation mode on all RMPs. This condition, if 
not corrected, could lead to total loss of control of radio 
communications, including the loss of communications, transponder 
functionality, standby navigation, or any combination of these. To 
address this condition, Airbus designed and certified modification 
211442 (install wiring and software L4.3 standard for digital audio) 
and published service information that provides instructions for 
installing that modification on in-service airplanes; EASA AD 2025-0286 
retains the AFM and MEL requirements of EASA AD 2025-0043R1 and adds a 
requirement to modify the airplane.
    This proposed AD would reduce the applicability and only apply to 
certain Model A330-941 airplanes. Airbus SAS Model A330-243, -243F, and 
-841 airplanes are not affected by the identified unsafe condition. The 
FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these 
products.
    You may examine the MCAI in the AD docket at regulations.gov under 
Docket No. FAA-2026-11813.

Material Incorporated by Reference Under 1 CFR Part 51

    EASA AD 2025-0286 specifies procedures for modifying the airplane 
by installing wiring and software (the digital radio and audio 
integrating management system (DRAIMS) L4.3 configuration). EASA AD 
2025-0286 also specifies revising the AFM and the MEL and, after the 
modification is accomplished, prohibits installing affected parts.
    This material is reasonably available because the interested 
parties have access to it through their normal course of business or by 
the means identified in the ADDRESSES section.

FAA's Determination

    These products have been approved by the civil aviation authority 
of another country and are approved for operation in the United States. 
Pursuant to the FAA's bilateral agreement with this State of Design 
Authority, that authority has notified the FAA of the unsafe condition 
described in the MCAI referenced above. The FAA is issuing this NPRM 
after determining that the unsafe condition described previously is 
likely to exist or develop on other products of the same type design.

Proposed AD Requirements in This NPRM

    This proposed AD would retain all requirements of AD 2025-09-07 and 
reduce the applicability of AD 2025-09-07. This proposed AD would also 
require accomplishing the modification specified in EASA AD 2025-0286 
described previously, except for any differences identified as 
exceptions in the regulatory text of this proposed AD. Accomplishing 
that modification would terminate the retained AFM and MEL revision 
requirements. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of 
affected parts under certain conditions. See ``Differences Between This 
Proposed AD and the MCAI'' for a discussion of the general differences 
included in this AD.

Differences Between This Proposed AD and the MCAI

    This proposed AD does not adopt paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of 
EASA AD 2025-0286 (EASA's retained AFM and master minimum equipment 
list requirements). Instead, this proposed AD retains and restates the 
corresponding AFM and MEL revision requirements of AD 2025-09-07 in 
paragraphs (g) and (h) of this AD.

Explanation of Required Compliance Information

    In the FAA's ongoing efforts to improve the efficiency of the AD 
process, the FAA developed a process to use some civil aviation 
authority (CAA) ADs as the primary source of information for compliance 
with requirements for corresponding FAA ADs. The FAA has been 
coordinating this process with manufacturers and CAAs. As a result, the 
FAA proposes to incorporate EASA AD 2025-0286 by reference in the FAA 
final rule. This proposed AD would, therefore, require compliance with 
EASA AD 2025-0286 in its entirety through that incorporation, except 
for any differences identified as exceptions in the regulatory text of 
this proposed AD. Using common terms that are the same as the heading 
of a particular section in EASA AD 2025-0286 does not mean that 
operators need comply only with that section. For example, where the AD 
requirement refers to ``all required actions and compliance times,'' 
compliance with this AD requirement is not limited to the section 
titled ``Required Action(s) and Compliance Time(s)'' in EASA AD 2025-
0286. Material required by EASA AD 2025-0286 is available at 
regulations.gov by searching for and locating Docket No. FAA-2026-11813 
after the FAA final rule is published.

Costs of Compliance

    The FAA estimates that this AD, if adopted as proposed, would 
affect 12 airplanes of U.S. registry. The FAA estimates the following 
costs to comply with this proposed AD:

[[Page 66018]]



                                      Estimated Costs for Required Actions
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                                                       Cost per    Cost on U.S.
                  Action                            Labor cost           Parts cost    product       operators
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Retained actions from AD 2025-09-07......  2 work-hours x $85 per hour           $0         $170          $2,040
                                            = $170.
New proposed actions.....................  6 work-hours x $85 per hour        1,242        1,752          21,024
                                            = $510.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Authority for This Rulemaking

    Title 49 of the United States Code specifies the FAA's authority to 
issue rules on aviation safety. Subtitle I, section 106, describes the 
authority of the FAA Administrator. Subtitle VII: Aviation Programs, 
describes in more detail the scope of the Agency's authority.
    The FAA is issuing this rulemaking under the authority described in 
Subtitle VII, Part A, Subpart III, Section 44701: General requirements. 
Under that section, Congress charges the FAA with promoting safe flight 
of civil aircraft in air commerce by prescribing regulations for 
practices, methods, and procedures the Administrator finds necessary 
for safety in air commerce. This regulation is within the scope of that 
authority because it addresses an unsafe condition that is likely to 
exist or develop on products identified in this rulemaking action.

Regulatory Findings

    The FAA determined that this proposed AD would not have federalism 
implications under Executive Order 13132. This proposed AD would not 
have a substantial direct effect on the States, on the relationship 
between the national government and the States, or on the distribution 
of power and responsibilities among the various levels of government.
    For the reasons discussed above, I certify this proposed 
regulation:
    (1) Is not a ``significant regulatory action'' under Executive 
Order 12866,
    (2) Would not affect intrastate aviation in Alaska, and
    (3) Would not have a significant economic impact, positive or 
negative, on a substantial number of small entities under the criteria 
of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.

List of Subjects in 14 CFR Part 39

    Air transportation, Aircraft, Aviation safety, Incorporation by 
reference, Safety.

The Proposed Amendment

    Accordingly, under the authority delegated to me by the 
Administrator, the FAA proposes to amend 14 CFR part 39 as follows:

PART 39--AIRWORTHINESS DIRECTIVES

0
1. The authority citation for part 39 continues to read as follows:

    Authority: 49 U.S.C. 106(g), 40113, 44701.


Sec.  39.13  [Amended]

0
2. The FAA amends Sec.  39.13 by:
0
a. Removing Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-09-07, Amendment 39-23028 
(90 FR 17888, April 30, 2025); and
0
b. Adding the following new AD:

Airbus SAS: Docket No. FAA-2026-11813; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-
01835-T.

(a) Comments Due Date

    The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive 
(AD) by December 3, 2026.

(b) Affected ADs

    This AD replaces AD 2025-09-07, Amendment 39-23028 (90 FR 17888, 
April 30, 2025) (AD 2025-09-07).

(c) Applicability

    This AD applies to Airbus SAS Model A330-941 airplanes, 
certificated in any category, as identified in European Union 
Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) AD 2025-0286, dated December 17, 2025 
(EASA AD 2025-0286).

(d) Subject

    Air Transport Association (ATA) of America Code 23, 
Communications.

(e) Unsafe Condition

    This AD was prompted by reports of loss of data synchronization 
between the radio management panels (RMPs) and the audio management 
unit. The FAA is issuing this AD to address such loss of data 
synchronization, which can result in the loss of control of radio 
communication, uncommanded changes of transponder and Traffic Alert 
and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) settings, and the activation 
of standby navigation mode on all RMPs. The unsafe condition, if not 
addressed, could result in the total loss of radio communications if 
RMP 3 is inoperative prior to dispatch, including the loss of 
transponder functionality and standby navigation.

(f) Compliance

    Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, 
unless already done.

(g) Retained Airplane Flight Manual (AFM) Revision, With No Changes

    This paragraph restates the requirements of paragraph (g) of AD 
2025-09-07, with no changes. Within 7 days after May 15, 2025 (the 
effective date of AD 2025-09-07), revise the Emergency Procedures 
section of the existing AFM to include the information in figure 1 
to paragraph (g) of this AD. This may be done by inserting a copy of 
figure 1 to paragraph (g) of this AD into the existing AFM. Using a 
different document with information identical to that contained in 
figure 1 to paragraph (g) of this AD is acceptable for compliance 
with the requirements of this paragraph.

                Figure 1 to Paragraph (g)--AFM Procedure
------------------------------------------------------------------------
                  Dual loss of RMP data synchronization
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Switch off RMP 1 and RMP 2.
Note: When RMP 1 and RMP 2 are switched off:
    --The aural alerts are not available on loudspeakers.
    --The communication is only available on RMP 3.
Check communication, transponder, TCAS and radio navigation settings.
------------------------------------------------------------------------

(h) Retained Minimum Equipment List (MEL) Revision, With No Changes

    This paragraph restates the requirements of paragraph (h) of AD 
2025-09-07, with no changes. Before further flight after 
accomplishing the requirements of paragraph (g) of this AD, revise 
the existing FAA-approved MEL to prohibit airplane dispatch 
(operation) with an inoperative RMP 3 under the MEL item equivalent 
to FAA master minimum equipment list 23-81-01.

[[Page 66019]]

(i) Retained Credit for Previous Actions, With No Changes

    This paragraph restates the credit specified in paragraph (i) of 
AD 2025-09-07, with no changes.
    (1) This paragraph provides credit for the AFM revision required 
by paragraph (g) of this AD, if the revision was performed before 
May 15, 2025 (the effective date of AD 2025-09-07) using Airbus 
A330/A340 Operations Engineering Bulletin 58, issue 1.0, dated

e.title: Unsafe Condition
e.text:
This AD was prompted by reports of loss of data synchronization 
between the radio management panels (RMPs) and the audio management 
unit. The FAA is issuing this AD to address such loss of data 
synchronization, which can result in the loss of control of radio 
communication, uncommanded changes of transponder and Traffic Alert 
and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) settings, and the activation 
of standby navigation mode on all RMPs. The unsafe condition, if not 
addressed, could result in the total loss of radio communications if 
RMP 3 is inoperative prior to dispatch, including the loss of 
transponder functionality and standby navigation.

f.text:

g.title: Retained Airplane Flight Manual (AFM) Revision, With No Changes
g.text:
This paragraph restates the requirements of paragraph (g) of AD 
2025-09-07, with no changes. Within 7 days after May 15, 2025 (the 
effective date of AD 2025-09-07), revise the Emergency Procedures 
section of the existing AFM to include the information in figure 1 
to paragraph (g) of this AD. This may be done by inserting a copy of 
figure 1 to paragraph (g) of this AD into the existing AFM. Using a 
different document with information identical to that contained in 
figure 1 to paragraph (g) of this AD is acceptable for compliance 
with the requirements of this paragraph.

                Figure 1 to Paragraph (g)--AFM Procedure
------------------------------------------------------------------------
                  Dual loss of RMP data synchronization
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Switch off RMP 1 and RMP 2.
Note: When RMP 1 and RMP 2 are switched off:
    --The aural alerts are not available on loudspeakers.
    --The communication is only available on RMP 3.
Check communication, transponder, TCAS and radio navigation settings.
------------------------------------------------------------------------

rec.subject: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
rec.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 D-2 helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by certification test results of a certain common cargo hook beam (CCHB) on the affected helicopters, which revealed that the installed CCHB could result in fuel leakage following a survivable accident. This proposed AD would require modification of the CCHB and fuel system and installation of structural reinforcement. This proposed AD would also prohibit installing a certain CCHB on any helicopter. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 198 (Thursday, October 15, 2026)]
[Proposed Rules]
[Pages 65492-65494]
From the Federal Register Online via the Government Publishing Office [www.gpo.gov]
[FR Doc No: 2026-21123]


-----------------------------------------------------------------------

DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION

Federal Aviation Administration

14 CFR Part 39

[Docket No. FAA-2026-11812; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01222-R]
RIN 2120-AA64


Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH 
(AHD) Helicopters

AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), DOT.

ACTION: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) 
for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 D-2 
helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by certification test 
results of a certain common cargo hook beam (CCHB) on the affected 
helicopters, which revealed that the installed CCHB could result in 
fuel leakage following a survivable accident. This proposed AD would 
require modification of the CCHB and fuel system and installation of 
structural reinforcement. This proposed AD would also prohibit 
installing a certain CCHB on any helicopter. The FAA is proposing this 
AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

DATES: The FAA must receive comments on this NPRM by November 30, 2026.

ADDRESSES: You may send comments, using the procedures found in 14 CFR 
11.43 and 11.45, by any of the following methods:
     Federal eRulemaking Portal: Go to regulations.gov. Follow 
the instructions for submitting comments.
     Fax: (202) 493-2251.
     Mail: U.S. Department of Transportation, Docket 
Operations, M-30, West Building Ground Floor, Room W12-140, 1200 New 
Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590.
     Hand Delivery: Deliver to Mail address above between 9 
a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
    AD Docket: You may examine the AD docket at regulations.gov under 
Docket No. FAA-2026-11812; or in person at Docket Operations between 9 
a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. The AD 
docket contains this NPRM, the mandatory continuing airworthiness 
information (MCAI), any comments received, and other information. The 
street address for Docket Operations is listed above.
    Material Incorporated by Reference:
     For European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) material 
identified in this proposed AD, contact EASA, Konrad-Adenauer-Ufer 3, 
50668 Cologne, Germany; phone: +49 221 8999 000; email: 
[email protected]; website: easa.europa.eu. You may find the EASA 
material on the EASA website at ad.easa.europa.eu.
     You may view this material at the FAA, Airworthiness 
Products Section, Operational Safety Branch, 10101 Hillwood Parkway, 
Fort Worth, TX 76177. For information on the availability of this 
material at the FAA, call (817) 222-5110.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Promita Dey, Aviation Safety Engineer, 
FAA, 1600 Stewart Avenue, Suite 410, Westbury, NY 11590; phone: (316) 
946-4106; email: [email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

Comments Invited

    The FAA invites you to send any written relevant data, views, or 
arguments about this proposal. Send your comments using a method listed 
under ADDRESSES. Include ``Docket No. FAA-2026-11812; Project 
Identifier MCAI-2025-01222-R'' at the beginning of your comments. The 
most helpful comments reference a specific portion of the proposal, 
explain the reason for any recommended change, and include supporting 
data. The FAA will consider all comments received by the closing date 
and may amend this proposal because of those comments.
    Except for Confidential Business Information (CBI) as described in 
the following paragraph, and other information as described in 14 CFR 
11.35, the FAA will post all comments received, without change, to 
regulations.gov, including any personal information you provide. The 
agency will also post a report summarizing each substantive verbal 
contact received about this NPRM.

Confidential Business Information

    CBI is commercial or financial information that is both customarily 
and actually treated as private by its owner. Under the Freedom of 
Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), CBI is exempt from public 
disclosure. If your comments responsive to this NPRM contain commercial 
or financial information that is customarily treated as private, that 
you actually treat as private, and that is relevant or responsive to 
this NPRM, it is important that you clearly designate the submitted 
comments as CBI. Please mark each page of your submission containing 
CBI as ``PROPIN.'' The FAA will treat such marked submissions as 
confidential under the FOIA, and they will not be placed in the public 
docket of this NPRM. Submissions containing CBI should be sent to 
Promita Dey, Aviation Safety Engineer, FAA, 1600 Stewart Avenue, Suite 
410, Westbury, NY 11590. Any commentary that the FAA receives which is 
not specifically designated as CBI will be placed in the public docket 
for this rulemaking.

Background

    EASA, which is the Technical Agent for the Member States of the 
European Union, has issued EASA AD 2025-0153, dated July 18, 2025 (EASA 
AD 2025-0153) (also referred to as the MCAI), to correct an unsafe 
condition on all AHD Model MBB-BK117 D-2 helicopters, all variants. The 
MCAI states that certification testing of the CCHB installation on AHD 
Model MBB-BK117 D-3 and D-3m helicopters revealed that a survivable 
accident could result in fuel leakage. The MCAI further states that, 
due to design similarity, AHD

[[Page 65493]]

Model MBB-BK117 D-2 helicopters, all variants, could also be affected 
by the same unsafe condition.
    This condition, if not addressed, could lead to fuel leakage and a 
possible fire after a survivable accident involving a helicopter with a 
certain CCHB installed.
    You may examine the MCAI in the AD docket at regulations.gov under 
Docket No. FAA-2026-11812.

Material Incorporated by Reference Under 1 CFR Part 51

    The FAA reviewed EASA AD 2025-0153, which specifies procedures for 
modification of the CCHB and the fuel system and installation of 
structural reinforcement. EASA AD 2025-0153 also specifies that, as an 
alternative to the modification, operation of a helicopter with an 
affected CCHB part number L851M1301101 installed is prohibited.
    Additionally, EASA AD 2025-0153 specifies procedures to modify the 
helicopter by installing an improved cargo hook weighing system 
concurrently with the modification. EASA AD 2025-0153 also specifies 
that installation of an affected CCHB on any helicopter is prohibited.
    This material is reasonably available because the interested 
parties have access to it through their normal course of business or by 
the means identified in the ADDRESSES section.

FAA's Determination

    These products have been approved by the civil aviation authority 
(CAA) of another country and are approved for operation in the United 
States. Pursuant to the FAA's bilateral agreement with this State of 
Design Authority, that authority has notified the FAA of the unsafe 
condition described in the MCAI referenced above. The FAA is issuing 
this NPRM after determining that the unsafe condition described 
previously is likely to exist or develop on other products of the same 
type design.

Proposed AD Requirements in This NPRM

    This proposed AD would require accomplishing the actions specified 
in EASA AD 2025-0153, described previously, as incorporated by 
reference, except for any differences identified as exceptions in the 
regulatory text of this proposed AD.

Explanation of Required Compliance Information

    In the FAA's ongoing efforts to improve the efficiency of the AD 
process, the FAA developed a process to use some CAA ADs as the primary 
source of information for compliance with requirements for 
corresponding FAA ADs. The FAA has been coordinating this process with 
manufacturers and CAAs. As a result, the FAA proposes to incorporate 
EASA AD 2025-0153 by reference in the FAA final rule. This proposed AD 
would, therefore, require compliance with EASA AD 2025-0153 in its 
entirety through that incorporation, except for any differences 
identified as exceptions in the regulatory text of this proposed AD. 
Using common terms that are the same as the heading of a particular 
section in EASA AD 2025-0153 does not mean that operators need comply 
only with that section. For example, where the AD requirement refers to 
``all required actions and compliance times,'' compliance with this AD 
requirement is not limited to the section titled ``Required Action(s) 
and Compliance Time(s)'' in EASA AD 2025-0153. Material required by 
EASA AD 2025-0153 for compliance will be available at regulations.gov 
under Docket No. FAA-2026-11812 after the FAA final rule is published.

Costs of Compliance

    The FAA estimates that this AD, if adopted as proposed, would 
affect 28 helicopters of U.S. registry.
    The FAA estimates the following costs to comply with this proposed 
AD:

                                                 Estimated Costs
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                                                                Cost on U.S.
              Action                     Labor cost       Parts cost    Cost per product          operators
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Modify the fuel system............  75 work-hours x $85      $18,625  $25,000.............  $700,000.
                                     per hour = $6,375.
Install improved fuel pump          4 work-hours x $85        32,909  $33,249.............  $930,972.
 cartridge (4 per helicopter).       per hour = $340.
Modify helicopter Install new CCHB  Up to 11 work-hours      228,985  Up to $229,920......  Up to $6,437,760.
                                     x $85 per hour =
                                     $935.
Modify helicopter retrofit CCHB...  Up to 30 work-hours       10,636  Up to $13,186.......  Up to $369,208.
                                     x $85 per hour =
                                     $2,550.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Authority for This Rulemaking

    Title 49 of the United States Code specifies the FAA's authority to 
issue rules on aviation safety. Subtitle I, section 106, describes the 
authority of the FAA Administrator. Subtitle VII: Aviation Programs, 
describes in more detail the scope of the Agency's authority.
    The FAA is issuing this rulemaking under the authority described in 
Subtitle VII, Part A, Subpart III, Section 44701: General requirements. 
Under that section, Congress charges the FAA with promoting safe flight 
of civil aircraft in air commerce by prescribing regulations for 
practices, methods, and procedures the Administrator finds necessary 
for safety in air commerce. This regulation is within the scope of that 
authority because it addresses an unsafe condition that is likely to 
exist or develop on products identified in this rulemaking action.

Regulatory Findings

    The FAA determined that this proposed AD would not have federalism 
implications under Executive Order 13132. This proposed AD would not 
have a substantial direct effect on the States, on the relationship 
between the national government and the States, or on the distribution 
of power and responsibilities among the various levels of government.
    For the reasons discussed above, I certify this proposed 
regulation:
    (1) Is not a ``significant regulatory action'' under Executive 
Order 12866,
    (2) Would not affect intrastate aviation in Alaska, and
    (3) Would not have a significant economic impact, positive or 
negative, on a substantial number of small entities under the criteria 
of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.

List of Subjects in 14 CFR Part 39

    Air transportation, Aircraft, Aviation safety, Incorporation by 
reference, Safety.

The Proposed Amendment

    Accordingly, under the authority delegated to me by the 
Administrator, the FAA proposes to amend 14 CFR part 39 as follows:

[[Page 65494]]

PART 39--AIRWORTHINESS DIRECTIVES

0
1. The authority citation for part 39 continues to read as follows:

    Authority:  49 U.S.C. 106(g), 40113, 44701.


Sec.  39.13  [Amended]

0
2. The FAA amends Sec.  39.13 by adding the following new airworthiness 
directive:

Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD): Docket No. FAA-2026-
11812; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01222-R.

(a) Comments Due Date

    The FAA must receive comments on this airworthiness directive 
(AD) by November 30, 2026.

(b) Affected ADs

    None.

(c) Applicability

    This AD applies to all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) 
Model MBB-BK 117 D-2 helicopters, certificated in any category.

(d) Subject

    Joint Aircraft System Component (JASC) Code 2500, Cabin 
equipment/furnishings.

(e) Unsafe Condition

    This AD was prompted by certification test results of the 
installation of a certain common cargo hook beam (CCHB) identifying 
that the installed CCHB could result in fuel leakage following a 
survivable accident. The FAA is issuing this AD to prevent possible 
fuel leakage. The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could lead to 
fuel leakage and a possible fire after a survivable accident 
involving a helicopter equipped with a certain CCHB.

(f) Compliance

    Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, 
unless already done.

(g) Required Actions

    Except as specified in paragraphs (h) and (i) of this AD: Comply 
with all required actions and compliance times specified in, and in 
accordance with, European Union Aviation Safety Agency AD 2025-0153, 
dated July 18, 2025 (EASA AD 2025-0153).

(h) Exceptions to EASA AD 2025-0153

    (1) Where EASA AD 2025-0153 refers to its effective date, this 
AD requires using the effective date of this AD.
    (2) Where EASA AD 2025-0153 requires compliance in terms of 
flight hours, this AD requires using hours time-in-service.
    (3) Where the material referenced in EASA AD 2025-0153 specifies 
``discard'', this AD requires replacing that text with ``remove from 
service''.
    (4) Where the material referenced in EASA AD 2025-0153 specifies 
``check'', this AD requires replacing that text with ``inspect''.
    (5) This AD does not adopt the ``Remarks'' section of EASA AD 
2025-0153.

(i) No Reporting Requirement

    Although the material referenced in EASA AD 2025-0153 specifies 
to submit information to the manufacturer, this AD does not require 
that action.

(j) Alternative Methods of Compliance (AMOCs)

    (1) The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA, has the 
authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the 
procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19. In accordance with 14 CFR 39.19, 
send your request to your principal inspector or local Flight 
Standards District Office, as appropriate. If sending information 
directly to the manager of the International Validation Branch, send 
it to the attention of the person identified in paragraph (k) of 
this AD and email to: [email protected].
    (2) Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate 
principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager 
of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding 
district office.

(k) Additional Information

    For more information about this AD, contact Promita Dey, 
Aviation Safety Engineer, FAA, 1600 Stewart Avenue, Suite 410, 
Westbury, NY 11590; phone: (316) 946-4106; email: 
[email protected].

equipment/furnishings.

e.title: Unsafe Condition
e.text:
This AD was prompted by certification test results of the 
installation of a certain common cargo hook beam (CCHB) identifying 
that the installed CCHB could result in fuel leakage following a 
survivable accident. The FAA is issuing this AD to prevent possible 
fuel leakage. The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could lead to 
fuel leakage and a possible fire after a survivable accident 
involving a helicopter equipped with a certain CCHB.

f.title: Compliance
f.text:

unless already done.

g.text:
Except as specified in paragraphs (h) and (i) of this AD: Comply 
with all required actions and compliance times specified in, and in 
accordance with, European Union Aviation Safety Agency AD 2025-0153, 
dated July 18, 2025 (EASA AD 2025-0153).

AD requires using the effective date of this AD.

``check'', this AD requires replacing that text with ``inspect''.

2025-0153.

Airworthiness Directives; Leonardo S.p.a. Helicopters

AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), DOT.

ACTION: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 
2024-05-06, which applies to all Leonardo S.p.a Model AW169 
helicopters. AD 2024-05-06 requires revising the airworthiness 
limitations section (ALS) of the existing helicopter maintenance manual 
(MM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing 
approved maintenance or inspection program for the helicopter. Since 
the FAA issued AD 2024-05-06, it was determined that incorrect material 
was referenced to revise the ALS. This proposed AD would require 
revising the ALS of the existing MM or ICA and the existing approved 
maintenance or inspection program. The FAA is proposing this AD to 
address the unsafe condition on these products.

DATES: The FAA must receive comments on this proposed AD by November 
30, 2026.

ADDRESSES: You may send comments, using the procedures found in 14 CFR 
11.43 and 11.45, by any of the following methods:
     Federal eRulemaking Portal: Go to regulations.gov. Follow 
the instructions for submitting comments.
     Fax: (202) 493-2251.
     Mail: U.S. Department of Transportation, Docket 
Operations, M-30, West Building Ground Floor, Room W12-140, 1200 New 
Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590.
     Hand Delivery: Deliver to Mail address above between 9 
a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
    AD Docket: You may examine the AD docket at regulations.gov under 
Docket No. FAA-2026-11808; or in person at Docket Operations between 9 
a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. The AD 
docket contains this NPRM, any comments received, and other 
information. The street address for Docket Operations is listed above.

[[Page 65141]]

    Material Incorporated by Reference:
     For Leonardo S.p.a. material identified in this proposed 
AD, contact Emanuele Bufano, Head of Airworthiness, Viale G. Agusta 
520, 21017 C. Costa di Samarate (Va) Italy; phone: +39 0331-225074; 
fax: +39 0331-229046; or at: customerportal.leonardocompany.com/en-US/.
     You may view this material at the FAA, Airworthiness 
Products Section, Operational Safety Branch, 10101 Hillwood Parkway, 
Fort Worth, TX 76177. For information on the availability of this 
material at the FAA, call (817) 222-5110.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Anthony Kenward, Aviation Safety 
Engineer, FAA, 1600 Stewart Avenue, Suite 410, Westbury, NY 11590; 
phone: (817) 222-4130; email: [email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

Comments Invited

    The FAA invites you to send any written relevant data, views, or 
arguments about this proposal. Send your comments using a method listed 
under ADDRESSES. Include ``Docket No. FAA-2026-11808; Project 
Identifier AD-2026-00520-R'' at the beginning of your comments. The 
most helpful comments reference a specific portion of the proposal, 
explain the reason for any recommended change, and include supporting 
data. The FAA will consider all comments received by the closing date 
and may revise this proposal because of those comments.
    Except for Confidential Business Information (CBI) as described in 
the following paragraph, and other information as described in 14 CFR 
11.35, the FAA will post all comments received, without change, to 
regulations.gov, including any personal information you provide. The 
agency will also post a report summarizing each substantive verbal 
contact received about this NPRM.

Confidential Business Information

    CBI is commercial or financial information that is both customarily 
and actually treated as private by its owner. Under the Freedom of 
Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), CBI is exempt from public 
disclosure. If your comments responsive to this NPRM contain commercial 
or financial information that is customarily treated as private, that 
you actually treat as private, and that is relevant or responsive to 
this NPRM, it is important that you clearly designate the submitted 
comments as CBI. Please mark each page of your submission containing 
CBI as ``PROPIN.'' The FAA will treat such marked submissions as 
confidential under the FOIA, and they will not be placed in the public 
docket of this NPRM. Submissions containing CBI should be sent to 
Anthony Kenward, Aviation Safety Engineer, FAA, 1600 Stewart Avenue, 
Suite 410, Westbury, NY 11590. Any commentary that the FAA receives 
which is not specifically designated as CBI will be placed in the 
public docket for this rulemaking.

Background

    The FAA issued AD 2024-05-06, Amendment 39-22697 (89 FR 24682, 
April 9, 2024) (AD 2024-05-06), for all Leonardo S.p.a. Model AW169 
helicopters. AD 2024-05-06 was prompted by a determination that new or 
more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. AD 2024-05-06 
requires revising the ALS of the existing helicopter maintenance manual 
or ICA and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as 
applicable. The FAA issued AD 2024-05-06 to address fatigue cracking, 
damage, and corrosion in principal structural elements.

Actions Since AD 2024-05-06 Was Issued

    Since the FAA issued AD 2024-05-06, the FAA determined that 
incorrect material was referenced for revising the ALS in AD 2024-05-
06. Furthermore, the material that was referenced in AD 2024-05-06 was 
not FAA-approved. As a result, the FAA determined that an appropriate 
FAA-approved ALS document is needed to address the unsafe condition. 
This proposed AD would reference the correct document.

FAA's Determination

    The products have been approved by the civil aviation authority of 
another country and are approved for operation in the United States. 
Pursuant to the FAA's bilateral agreement with this State of Design 
Authority, that authority has notified the FAA of the unsafe condition 
described in the material referenced above. The FAA is issuing this 
NPRM after determining that the unsafe condition described previously 
is likely to exist or develop on other products of the same type 
design.

Material Incorporated by Reference Under 1 CFR Part 51

    The FAA reviewed Leonardo AW169 # AMPI Chapter 4 Issue 6, Document 
No. 169F0255A075, Issue A, dated October 17, 2025, which specifies 
procedures for revising the airworthiness limitations, tasks, and 
associated thresholds and intervals for various parts, and specifies 
new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations for certain 
components installed on the helicopter.
    This material is reasonably available because the interested 
parties have access to it through their normal course of business or by 
the means identified in the ADDRESSES section.

Proposed AD Requirements in This NPRM

    This proposed AD would require revising the ALS of the existing 
helicopter maintenance manual or ICA and the existing approved 
maintenance or inspection program, as applicable.

Costs of Compliance

    The FAA estimates that this AD, if adopted as proposed, would 
affect 18 helicopters of U.S. registry.
    The FAA estimates the following costs to comply with this proposed 
AD:

                                                 Estimated Costs
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                                                         Cost per   Cost on U.S.
                   Action                              Labor cost           Parts cost    product     operators
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Revise the ALS.............................  1 work-hour x $85 per hour =           $0         $85        $1,530
                                              $85.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Authority for This Rulemaking

    Title 49 of the United States Code specifies the FAA's authority to 
issue rules on aviation safety. Subtitle I, section 106, describes the 
authority of the FAA Administrator. Subtitle VII, Aviation Programs, 
describes in more detail the scope of the Agency's authority.
    The FAA is issuing this rulemaking under the authority described in 
Subtitle VII, Part A, Subpart III, Section 44701: General requirements. 
Under that section, Congress charges the FAA

[[Page 65142]]

with promoting safe flight of civil aircraft in air commerce by 
prescribing regulations for practices, methods, and procedures the 
Administrator finds necessary for safety in air commerce. This 
regulation is within the scope of that authority because it addresses 
an unsafe condition that is likely to exist or develop on products 
identified in this rulemaking action.

Regulatory Findings

    The FAA determined that this proposed AD would not have federalism 
implications under Executive Order 13132. This proposed AD would not 
have a substantial direct effect on the States, on the relationship 
between the national government and the States, or on the distribution 
of power and responsibilities among the various levels of government.
    For the reasons discussed above, I certify that the proposed 
regulation:
    (1) Is not a ``significant regulatory action'' under Executive 
Order 12866,
    (2) Would not affect intrastate aviation in Alaska, and
    (3) Would not have a significant economic impact, positive or 
negative, on a substantial number of small entities under the criteria 
of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.

List of Subjects in 14 CFR Part 39

    Air transportation, Aircraft, Aviation safety, Incorporation by 
reference, Safety.

The Proposed Amendment

    Accordingly, under the authority delegated to me by the 
Administrator, the FAA proposes to amend 14 CFR part 39 as follows:

PART 39--AIRWORTHINESS DIRECTIVES

0
1. The authority citation for part 39 continues to read as follows:

    Authority: 49 U.S.C. 106(g), 40113, 44701.


Sec.  39.13  [Amended]

0
